theHEADLINE: BOTH BLOCKERS ARE GENUINELY CLEARED, AND THE ONE THAT MATTERED IS DIAGNOSED CORRECTLY. I recomputed the Unicode fact exhaustively rather than sampling it: over all 1,112,064 valid scalars, UTF-8 byte order and scalar-value order have ZERO inversions -- they are one total order -- while UTF-16 has exactly one, at U+FFFF vs U+10000. v6 does not merely rename the encoding. It identifies the defect as a VACUOUS caveat -- a disclosed limitation that could not exist -- and correctly names what the vacuous caveat DISPLACED. I verified every link of that displacement chain independently and every link holds: canonical-json-profile.v1 states the fact correctly and UR-1 is genuinely open; delivery.v4 is APPLIED per freeze section 3; it resolves to delivery.v2, whose releaseManifestSchema.canonicalization is RFC 8785 JCS; and JCS sorts by UTF-16 code units. The settling vector reproduces exactly. v6 broke none of v5's cryptography: I resolved the full chain and leaf-diffed it -- 3 leaves changed out of 2520, key sets identical, not one of the three under any recipe, vector or pin, and not one hex digest token anywhere in a from- or value-field.

B-EIR5-02-theVacuousOrderingCaveat.claimUnderTest: v5 asserted, in a v5-AUTHORED block, that key-sort by Unicode scalar value and key-sort by UTF-8 bytes 'differ above the BMP'.

iVerifiedTheFactEXHAUSTIVELYRatherThanBy.domain: All valid Unicode scalars: 0x0000-0x10FFFF excluding the surrogate range D800-DFFF. Count measured, not quoted: 1112064. This matches the figure v6 publishes.
iVerifiedTheFactEXHAUSTIVELYRatherThanBy.utf8VersusScalarOnSINGLECHARACTERS: Encoded every one of the 1112064 scalars to UTF-8 and compared each to its scalar-order predecessor. ADJACENT INVERSIONS: 0. Because a strictly increasing map on a totally ordered chain is order-preserving throughout, zero adjacent inversions establishes the two are the SAME TOTAL ORDER, not merely locally agreeing. UTF-8 is order-preserving by construction.
iVerifiedTheFactEXHAUSTIVELYRatherThanBy.utf8VersusScalarOnSTRINGS: Also verified at the string level, because key-sorting compares strings and not characters. (a) A full cross-product of 2-character strings over 17 boundary scalars spanning every UTF-8 length transition and both sides of the surrogate gap and the BMP edge -- U+0000, U+0001, U+007F, U+0080, U+07FF, U+0800, U+D7FF, U+E000, U+E001, U+FFFD, U+FFFE, U+FFFF, U+10000, U+10001, U+1F600, U+10FFFE, U+10FFFF -- 83521 ordered pairs, MISMATCHES: 0. (b) 400000 random string pairs of lengths 0-3 drawn uniformly from the full valid scalar set, MISMATCHES: 0.
iVerifiedTheFactEXHAUSTIVELYRatherThanBy.utf16: Encoded every scalar to UTF-16 code units and to UTF-16BE bytes. ADJACENT INVERSIONS: exactly 1, in both representations, at U+FFFF versus U+10000. Exactly as v6 states.
iVerifiedTheFactEXHAUSTIVELYRatherThanBy.conclusion: The v5 sentence is FALSE. The two policies it named are ONE policy. CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY.

theSETTLINGVECTORReproduces.firstDivergence: The largest scalar x below U+10000 for which UTF-16 places U+10000 first is U+FFFF, confirming 'first differing at U+FFFF vs U+10000'.

judgingV6sFRAMINGOfTheDefect.theQuestion: Is the defect a misnamed encoding, or is it that the caveat was VACUOUS and DISPLACED the real undetermined pair?
judgingV6sFRAMINGOfTheDefect.myFinding: v6's framing is CORRECT, and it is the stronger and more useful diagnosis. A misnaming would be a typo with a one-word fix. What actually happened is worse in kind: the sentence existed to DISCLOSE A LIMITATION, and the limitation it disclosed cannot exist, because the two candidate policies it offered to discriminate between are the same policy. There was never anything to discriminate. A reader who accepted the caveat came away believing an ordering risk had been disclosed when none had been. That is why it survived four independent reviews -- it reads as a concession, and reviewers audit claims of merit, not admissions of limit. The corpus's own freeze reaches the same conclusion at section 7.2.2.1 and adds the correct standing rule: a caveat is a measurement, recompute limitations too. I reached the arithmetic independently before reading that section and it agrees.
judgingV6sFRAMINGOfTheDefect.andTheDISPLACEMENTIsRealNotRhetorical: The genuinely undetermined pair is {scalar value == UTF-8 bytes} versus {UTF-16 code units}. That pair is live, named and open in the corpus. So the false caveat did not merely fail to inform -- it occupied the sentence where the true caveat belonged, and spent the reader's trust doing it.
judgingV6sFRAMINGOfTheDefect.theREPLACEMENTIsTRUE: I checked that the new caveat is not vacuous in its turn. The EP8-POS-NOMATCH-PASS bundle is pure ASCII. For ASCII keys, scalar order, UTF-8 order AND UTF-16 order all coincide, so the reproduction genuinely CANNOT discriminate scalar/UTF-8 from UTF-16. The replacement discloses a limitation that really exists. This is the exact remedy the v5 reviewer specified.

advisories.theTension: So all six BND vectors are 'new' only relative to v1; relative to v5's own predecessor, nothing in the five arrays is new. The same seven-item list uses 'carried byte-identical from v4' at item 0 and 'NEW IN v5 UNDER COORDINATOR COMMISSION' at item 6, which trains the reader to read 'new' as 'new in v5'. Under that reading 'plus 6 new ones' is false, and it is contradicted by v5's own totals block.
advisories.whyThisIsNOTABlocker: The v5 reviewer's remedy was specifically 'derive the two figures from the arrays they count, or delete them'. Both figures are now exact properties of published arrays -- 32 is the sum of the five, 6 is the length of the BND array -- and the sentence is internally consistent at 26+6=32 with the 7 corpus reproductions independently confirmed. The descriptive clause is also true: the six BND vectors are exactly the ones that make the restored text-component clauses falsifiable. The residue is one unanchored adjective, not a wrong number, and the blocker was about the numbers.
advisories.recommendation: In any successor, anchor the word: 'plus the six BND text-component vectors, new since v1 (four in v2, two in v3)'. That removes the last figure in this sentence whose truth depends on knowing which version it is measured against.

advisories.title: The resolved v6 document inherits one census figure that is a property of v5's emitted file and of no v6 artifact
advisories.measured: v5's emittedFileLeafCensus publishes emittedFileByteLength = '287480'. Resolving v6 full-chain changes three string leaves, so the resolved document is not 287480 bytes under any serialisation. The other census figures survive intact and I verified each: totalLeaves 2520 and stringLeaves 2520 both still measure exactly, jsonNumberLeaves/jsonBooleanLeaves/jsonNullLeaves/nonStringObjectKeys/duplicateKeysOnReparse all still 0, and stalenessSweepOccurrencesOutsideQuotationSites still 0.
advisories.whyThisIsNOTABlocker: Three independent reasons. (1) The v5 reviewer expressly ruled it out of scope: 'NO CENSUS FIGURE ... NEEDS TO MOVE. I checked all of them and they are right', and warned that a v6 touching anything further would be rejected. v6 obeyed. (2) A resolved delta has no canonical serialisation -- indent, separators and key order are all unfixed -- so emittedFileByteLength is not even computable for it; the figure is well-defined only for an emitted file, and v5's emitted file still exists unchanged at its pinned digest. (3) The corpus has already settled this residual class in the opposite direction from a blocker: freeze section 3's C-2 row records that the resolved effective contract 'still names check-c2-v9.py, so the artifact's own statement of its instrument now disagrees with this row -- section 7.2 forbids editing the reviewed bytes, so it is RECORDED rather than patched'. The DELIVERY row records the identical pattern for retainedChecker.path.
advisories.recommendation: Nothing to change in v6. Recorded here so the residual is on the record rather than discovered later, per the convention those two rows establish. If this lineage is ever emitted as a whole document again rather than as a delta, the byte length must be re-derived at that fixed point.

advisories.title: UR-1 is cited with a dot path into what is actually a JSON array
advisories.measured: v6 cites 'canonical-json-profile.v1#$.undeterminedRegister.UR-1' at three places. $.undeterminedRegister is a LIST of 5 objects identified by an 'id' field, so the strict path is $.undeterminedRegister[0], or $.undeterminedRegister[?(@.id=='UR-1')] if position is not to be relied on. The dot form does not resolve literally.
advisories.impact: None on correctness. 'UR-1' occurs exactly once in the register so the referent is unambiguous. v6 inherited the citation form verbatim from freeze section 7.2.2.1, which uses the same shape. Flagged only because this corpus has been bitten repeatedly by paths that look resolvable and are not.

advisories.title: One quoted reason is attributed to two diff-manifest rows but belongs to only one
advisories.measured: v6 writes that the v5 diff manifest 'edited items 0 and 6 of this very list for the stated reason "the adds-list must describe v5, not v4"'. That quoted reason is the stated reason of the item-6 row only. The item-0 row's stated reason is 'updated to name the carry rather than claim novelty'.
advisories.impact: None on the argument. The load-bearing claim -- that both neighbours were edited and item 3 was not -- is exactly correct, and I verified it against carriedBlockDiffManifest block 11 directly.

advisories.title: Both replacement values contain an ungrammatical 'and nor ... from ...' construction
advisories.measured: Both new values read '...cannot distinguish escaping policies for non-ASCII, and nor key-sort by Unicode scalar value from key-sort by UTF-16 code units.' The verb 'cannot distinguish' is elided across 'nor', which does not license the trailing 'from' complement.
advisories.impact: None on meaning or on the technical content, which I verified is correct. Worth a copy-edit in any successor because this is a sentence four reviews already failed to read carefully.

advisories.title: The delivery canonicalisation is paraphrased slightly short
advisories.measured: v6 renders it as 'sha256 over JCS'. The actual definition in delivery.v2 is sha256 over a domain-separated preimage: UTF8('opensip.release-manifest.v1\u0000') || JCS(manifest with manifestId and signatures omitted).
advisories.impact: None on the hazard being argued. The domain prefix and the omission rule do not affect whether JCS's UTF-16 key ordering is load-bearing in the preimage -- it is. Noted for precision only.

It does mean my verdict on v5's cryptography is INHERITED from the v5 independent review, not re-earned.

check-evidence-v10.py and check-evidence-v11.py were NOT run to completion -- both exceeded a 120-second timeout and I killed them. I therefore have NO result from them, favourable or otherwise, and I am not reporting one. I did confirm that no .py file in artifacts/ mentions evidence-identity-recipes at all, so neither is a checker for this lineage.

I did NOT read RFC 8785 itself -- no network access was used in this review. The claim that JCS sorts by UTF-16 code units rests on my own knowledge plus two corroborating corpus witnesses (canonical-json-profile.v1's jcsHazardMeasured and orderingPlanes), which is weaker than reading the normative text.

The UTF-8/scalar string-order equivalence is exhaustive on SINGLE SCALARS (all 1,112,064) but NOT exhaustive on strings, which is an infinite set. String-level evidence is an 83,521-pair boundary cross-product and 400,000 random pairs, both with zero mismatches, plus the structural argument that UTF-8 is order-preserving by construction. I regard this as settled but the string case is argued, not enumerated.

I examined UR-1 closely and read the other four UR entries only for their open/closed state. I did NOT audit the rest of canonical-json-profile.v1 -- not its recipeRegistry, vectorIndex, workedExamples, discrepancyRegister or reproductionLog -- and I did NOT verify its own measuredSelfReport. reviewerPosition: PASS. I came to this looking for the fifth flat-read and for a repair that quietly edited reviewed bytes, and found neither. The two things that could have made this a REJECT were: a third site in v5 carrying the false sentence that 'site 1 of 2 / site 2 of 2' would have silently left behind, and a recipe or pin moving under cover of a prose fix. I checked both directly -- v5 carries exactly two sites and v6 repairs exactly those two, and the resolved document differs from v5 in 3 leaves out of 2520 with no hex token anywhere in the diff. The strongest thing I can say for v6 is that its central judgement is right and non-obvious: the defect was not a misnamed encoding but a caveat that disclosed a limitation which cannot exist, and which occupied the place where a real and still-open limitation belonged. That distinction is the difference between a typo and a four-review failure, and v6 gets it right. The strongest thing I can say against it is ADV-EIR6-01: the sentence at whatThisArtifactAdds[3] now has four correct, array-derivable figures joined by one adjective -- 'new' -- whose truth still depends on knowing which version you are measuring against, and v5's own totals block says plainly that nothing in that block is new. That is a smaller version of the same disease, and it is why I recorded it rather than waving it through, but it is not worth a tenth rejection of a lineage whose arithmetic no reviewer has been able to break.
